neet_che_u12_t04_1.working: Ni2+ is 3d8. Strong-field CN- pairs the electrons, leaving one 3d orbital empty. This gives dsp2 hybridisation, which is square planar.

neet_che_u12_t04_2.working: Fe2+ is d6. Strong-field CN- pairs all six electrons, so two inner 3d orbitals stay empty. Hybridisation is d2sp3, an inner-orbital complex. [CoF6]3- is sp3d2 (outer orbital). Ni(CO)4 and [CoCl4]2- are sp3, using no d orbitals.

neet_che_u12_t04_3.working: Co3+ is d6. F- is weak field, so the complex is high spin with 4 unpaired electrons. mu = sqrt(4 x 6) = sqrt(24) = 4.90 BM.

neet_che_u12_t04_4.working: Ni(CO)4 is sp3, tetrahedral and diamagnetic, so A is true. Ni is in the 0 oxidation state (3d8 4s2, rearranged to 3d10), not +2, so R is false.

neet_che_u12_t04_5.working: Fe3+ is d5. Low spin with CN- gives d2sp3 hybridisation and 1 unpaired electron, so mu = 1.73 BM and I is correct. NCERT lists among VBT's limitations that it cannot exactly predict tetrahedral versus square planar structures of 4-coordinate complexes, so II is correct.
